summary: Degraded-path routing sent user requests to initializing replica, causing p99 timeouts and 504s
description:
Issue summary: During a traffic spike on 2026-03-12 ~14:10 UTC, a subset of inference requests for Acme Health were routed to replicas that were still initializing (cold-start path). Impact: elevated p99 latency (sustained >12s) and a spike in 504 gateway timeouts for ~18 minutes. This affected generation and chat endpoints for a pinned model and caused visible errors in Acme's customer-facing product.

Impact: Client-reported degradation for live triage workflow; ~8% of requests from the customer's production traffic returned 504 or timed out. No token-level errors observed from the model itself.

Environment: Production (dedicated pool for Acme Health), region: us-east-1. Model pinned by customer: acme-rlhf-2026-01 (variant: quantized-int8).

Observed behavior: Routing algorithm diverted traffic to replicas in a degraded-path group rather than queuing for healthy warm replicas. Initializing replicas accepted requests before KV cache warmup and GPU memory allocations completed, producing long-tail latency and gateway 504s.

Expected behavior: Requests should be routed to ready replicas (or queued/fail-fast to an alternative fallback) and initializing replicas should not accept production requests until KV cache warmups are complete.

Relevant links: Grafana latency dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/acme/latency?from=2026-03-12T14:00Z&to=2026-03-12T14:30Z, Kibana request sample: https://kibana.internal.redwood/logs?q=SUP-91827
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated pool with pinned model acme-rlhf-2026-01 and configure canary/policy allowing degraded-path fallbacks.
2) Simulate a 3x traffic burst to the pool sustaining 350 RPS for 5 minutes (use synthetic load: /debug/loadgen with customer headers).
3) Observe routing decisions from the router service and identify replicas that transition from 'initializing' to 'accepting' while KV cache is empty.
4) Measure p50/p95/p99 for generation endpoint and check for 504 gateway responses during the burst.

comments: Evelyn Park (2026-03-12T14:22Z): Customer reported high p99 and 504s affecting triage flow; provided Grafana links and sample request IDs; customer asked for ETA on mitigation.
Priya Shah (2026-03-12T14:35Z): Acknowledged, triaging with SRE. Preliminary metric shows routing to initializing replicas around 14:11-14:29 UTC. Added routing and serving-runtime oncall.

SRE oncall - Marcus Nguyen (2026-03-12T14:48Z): Observed that router's health scoring briefly considered initializing replicas as acceptable due to stale health cache; created a short-term rule to block 'initializing' state from routing.
Customer (Acme Health - Lina Morales) (2026-03-12T15:05Z): Confirmed errors decreased after mitigation; still seeing intermittent slow requests. Asked whether requests were replayed or lost.
Priya Shah (2026-03-12T15:12Z): Confirmed we will not replay user requests automatically; we implemented a routing block and are gathering post-mitigation telemetry. Follow-up planned for postmortem.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Health cache staleness allowed 'initializing' replicas into candidate set for routing during sudden traffic spike.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler added replicas in parallel without completing KV cache warmups; router evaluated capacity availability and chose degraded-path routing logic that prefers quicker acceptance over readiness.
Metric finding: p99 jumped from 1.2s to 13.8s for affected endpoint between 14:10-14:28 UTC. 504 count rose from baseline 0.2% to 7.9% of requests for the customer's pool.
Log correlation: Several request IDs routed to replica-73d2 show kv_cache_miss=true and warmup_stage=0 — replica accepted requests while warmup incomplete.
Temporary mitigation: Router rule updated at 14:39Z to exclude replicas with state!=ready; this reduced 504s to <0.5% for the customer within 5 minutes.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary): Router configuration adjusted to disallow routing to replicas in 'initializing' or 'warming' states. Autoscaler workflow updated to annotate new replicas as 'draining-accepting' until KV warmup completes. Permanent fix scheduled: router health cache TTL reduction and adding explicit warmup-complete signal to replica registration. Postmortem and follow-ups created.
resolution_notes: Rollout notes: Config change deployed via canary to routing cluster at 2026-03-12T14:39Z; monitored for 20m before full rollout.
Follow-ups: INT-4421 created to add warmup-complete RPC handshake; SRE task assigned to reduce health cache TTL (INT-4473).
Customer communication: Notified Acme Health of mitigation and planned permanent fixes; scheduled postmortem sync on 2026-03-15.
